references.title: OpenMouse mouse-protocol (Razer codec, product table, captures)

use.purpose: Control channel: 90-byte feature report 0 on the interface whose only collection is Generic Desktop Mouse; Razer does not declare it in the descriptor

linux.notes: Needs a udev rule for hidraw

macos.notes: The browser needs Input Monitoring permission to open mouse-class interfaces (OpenMouse)

limitations: Generated from OpenMouse mouse-protocol @e53af6d5: src/razer/devices.ts (third_party/openmouse/razer-devices.ts) and src/razer/codec.ts.
Nothing here has been verified on hardware by UDB.

Razer’s protocol is not self-describing: the transaction ID, polling command and DPI ceiling come from OpenMouse’s audit of OpenRazer, per product ID. A wrong transaction ID means the mouse does not answer; nothing is written.
On a receiver, two interfaces can look identical; UDB tries each granted mouse interface until one answers.
DPI stages, lift-off, button mapping and lighting are not implemented. The serial number is never read.
